general_information.Pre-Requisite: Recommend to have knowledge of circuit theory (see CEC201) in advance
general_information.Description: This course introduces mainly basic concepts of semiconductor devices including diodes, bipolar junction transistors (BJTs), field effect transistors (FETs). In each device; its analysis is first presented after a particular device physics overview, then the design and some circuit applications follow. The main focus of this course is not only to develop the student ability to analyze and design basic analog electronic circuits with passive components and/or the active elements like diode and transistors. But also, some experiments are provided to help students to have a thorough grasp of the basic electronic circuit problems. Topic covered: Semiconductor Diodes, Diode Applications, Bipolar Junction Transistors, DC Biasing-BJTs, BJT AC Analysis, Field-Effect Transistors, FET Biasing and FET Amplifier.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend more than 80% of contact sessions in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Students must complete the lab sessions with the average passing grade. - Encouragingly access to the companion website http://wps.prenhall.com/boylestad/ for self-practice - Promptly access to the FU CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: Specific Tools: 1) Multisim Software (Student Edition) http://multisim.en.softonic.com/ 2) Lab equipments/ Training Kits - Oscilloscope and Function generator - Kit 1: Semiconductor Characteristics - Kit 2: Half wave, full wave and bridge rectifiers - Kit 3: Characteristics of transistors (CB,CC, CE) - Kit 4: Transistor Amplifier(CB, CC, CE), Bootstraping Amplifier, Cascode Amplifier, Emitter Follower (CC). Note: All kits are imported from Kitek Technologies Private Limited, India.

assessments.Question Type: Circuit analysis using circuit analysis tool
assessments.Grading Guide: - by instructors and done by every group of 4 students - Submit file of design by groups - Write technical reports to describe and evaluate their designs
assessments.Note: - Suggesstion: Instructor can assign some student to use Multisim/Pspice to design analog circuits using semiconductor devices.

assessments.Duration: 90' for each experiment at Lab rooms
assessments.Question Type: Questions at the end of lab manuals
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Related respectively topics: Oscilloscope, Diodes, Rectifier, Transistors and FET Amplifier
assessments.Grading Guide: - 5 lab sessions are allocated suitably according to specific implementation condition of every campus - groups of 2-3 students are guided by instructors before doing experiments - perform step-by-step measurements or observation following lab manuals and take required data to process afterward. - A average grade of 5 in laboratory is required to pass the course.
assessments.Note: Lab manuals should be given to students at the beginning of the course Be aware that students will not be able to make up the lab. If students miss a lab they must either have a written doctor’s excuse or an excuse approved by your laboratory instructor to avoid having a score of zero recorded for the missed lab. Bring a calculator to the laboratory. The lab reports are normally collected right after the lab session.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice questions or suitable format
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Each Progess Test must cover generally all learned topics of the course.
assessments.Grading Guide: by instructors and by suitable means (computer or paper)
assessments.Note: Instruction and shedules for Progress tests must be presented in the Course Implementation Plan approved by the director of the campus. Instructor has responsibility to review the test for students after graded.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choice questions marked by computer
assessments.Note: No materials may be consulted during an exam unless specifically permitted by your instructor. A calculator is necessary for exams, but all memory must be erased.
